summary: Panel query parameter bindings reset when two users concurrently toggle pinned filters, causing orphaned tracehook tokens and missed alert context
description:
Issue summary:
When two users edit the same dashboard at the same time and one user toggles the 'Pinned Filters' toggle while the other is changing a panel's query parameter bindings, the panel's saved query binds ({{bind}}) are reset to defaults and the panel's tracehook token is replaced with a temporary token. This causes trace links in the panel to become orphaned and recent alert evaluations for that panel to run without the expected context attributes.

Impact:
- NovaForms reports missing trace links from dashboard panels for ~8% of requests after concurrent edits.
- Alerts tied to panel-context (e.g., request.user_id and route_id) evaluated without bindings, resulting in at least one false negative for a customer SLA alert during yesterday's maintenance window.
- Investigations show orphaned tracehook tokens and short-lived ephemeral token churn immediately after the concurrent edit event.

Environment:
prod/us-east (customer org id: org-4X9c) — dashboards served from console node pool c6g-console-2.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Two users open the same dashboard (dashboard id dsh-8112) in different browsers.
2) User A edits Panel #3 query to add a bound parameter (filter: route_id = {{route_id}}). User A clicks Save but does not change pinned filters.
3) While User A is still in the editor, User B toggles the dashboard-level 'Pinned Filters' switch on then off, and clicks Save.
4) User A completes the save.
5) Reload dashboard: Panel #3 now shows route_id bound to default 'all' and trace links report a temporary tracehook token (tracehook-temp-*) that does not map to any session in the trace ingestion logs.

Observed behavior:
- Panel-level query binding values revert to defaults.
- Tracehook token shown in panel link differs from the original and is not present in trace ingestion (orphaned).
- Alerts that depend on the panel query context fail to include the binding attributes and therefore do not fire correctly.

Expected behavior:
- Concurrent edits should merge with last-write-wins at a well-defined granularity without dropping panel-level bindings or replacing persistent tracehook tokens. Tracehook tokens in panel links should remain mapped to the panel's saved configuration and not be transiently replaced by ephemeral tokens.

Logs / Links / Evidence:
- Customer-provided screenshot: https://filebin.company/novaforms/snap-930271.png
- Console dashboard audit trail (excerpt): https://s3.console.redwood/logs/dsh-8112-audit-20260310.txt
- Support trace ingestion query (search for tracehook-temp-): link: https://redwood.query/trace?query=tracehook-temp-
comments: Support (Liam Chen) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Logged as P1 Sev1 and escalated to Console team. Asked customer for exact browser versions and the two user IDs involved.

Customer (NovaForms - Priya Desai) 2026-03-10: Provided user IDs (user-952, user-953) and browser details: Chrome 111 on macOS, Firefox 115 on Linux. Attached reproduction video and the dashboard JSON export.

Console Eng (Marco Liu) 2026-03-11: Initial hypothesis: concurrent dashboard-level metadata write is overwriting panel-level saved state object due to a merge key mismatch. Reproduced in staging with race condition when toggle change hits the update-v2 endpoint while panel save is in-flight.

SRE (Elena Park) 2026-03-11: Confirmed ephemeral tracehook tokens are created by the dashboard save code path when it detects an unresolved binding reference. We see token churn with a TTL of 5 minutes; tokens never persisted to the tracehook mapping table if save path was canceled/overwritten.

Support (Liam Chen) 2026-03-12: Customer accepted a temporary mitigation (avoid toggling pinned filters during concurrent edits). Requested an ETA for a code fix and whether we can retroactively reconcile orphaned tokens for the alert window.

Console Eng (Marco Liu) 2026-03-12: Working on a patch that serializes dashboard-level metadata updates and applies a merge strategy that preserves panel.bindings. Will propose a hotfix to prevent ephemeral token creation on concurrent writes.
investigation_notes:
Reproduction in staging: created 2 headless clients that simultaneously submitted edits. Observed update-v2 handler applies dashboard-level save last, which rewrites the saved_state object entirely when pinned_filters key exists. Root cause: the client sends 'saved_state' as a full object; server uses non-atomic upsert which replaces panel.bindings map when merge is partial. Additionally, tracehook token generation is triggered when binding placeholders are unresolved, and token persisting is on a separate background job which may be canceled when subsequent save overwrites the token_id field. Evidence: staging trace logs show a write sequence: saved_state -> token-gen -> token-persist canceled by subsequent replace.
Potential fix: change server to perform deep-merge for saved_state blob, and make token persist phase synchronous or transactional with the saved_state write.
Related PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/abc123 (WIP)
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied for affected customer: Support created a short policy guidance and a console-side banner that warns users about concurrent edits and instructs to avoid toggling pinned filters during edits. For the specific alert window, SRE was able to retroactively remap 72 orphaned tracehook tokens to their original panel config by cross-referencing the audit trail and temporarily re-inserting token mappings into the tracehook table.
Planned permanent fix: patch queued (PR abc123) to implement deep-merge upsert for dashboard saved_state and to make tracehook token persistence atomic. Targeted rollout to staging on 2026-03-15 and canary in prod us-east 2026-03-17. Post-deploy, we'll run a synthetic concurrent-edit regression test and monitor tracehook-token churn metrics for 48 hours.
Follow-ups: add automated test for concurrent dashboard edits, add an alert for abnormal token churn, and update runbook to include token reconciliation steps.
